points: **NICE NG243:** hyperpigmentation **may not be visible on black or brown skin** — ask whether the patient has noticed a change and **check the buccal mucosa and scars**.
**Adrenal crisis:** vomiting, abdominal pain, confusion, hypotension/shock — often triggered by intercurrent illness; can be fatal (the press cases).
people on oral glucocorticoids at physiological doses or above. **Inhaled, injected or topical steroids can lower the 9 am cortisol.** Wait 4 weeks after IM/intra-articular steroid injections.
**short Synacthen (ACTH stimulation) test**, ACTH, renin, **21-hydroxylase antibodies**, adrenal imaging if antibody-negative, very-long-chain fatty acids in young men.
**NICE NG243 (2024): offer an 8 am–9 am serum cortisol** to people with suspected AI (course teaching: 8 am cortisol). Interpretation for adults (modern immunoassays):
Measure **U&E** (Na⁺, K⁺), glucose, FBC, and **ACTH** with the cortisol sample if possible (local lab rules — EDTA, on ice). Check TFT and **renin/aldosterone**.

items.t: Vomiting, abdominal pain, confusion or collapse with suspected adrenal insufficiency: **adrenal crisis**, hydrocortisone 100 mg IM and 999.
Unexplained pigmentation with low sodium or high potassium: same-day 9am (or random) cortisol and endocrine advice.

pearls.t: "**Pigmented palmar creases and gums + salt craving + postural dizziness = check a 9 am cortisol today.**"
"**Sick-day rules save lives**" — rehearse them at every supply.
Pale patient with AI features on long-term steroids = **secondary/tertiary AI** — no pigmentation expected.
